GU₄.DA.UR.RA: GU₄.DA.UR.RA, a named kind of hired ox or ox-team (?), UNCERTAIN: a Sumerian-looking compound of GU₄ “ox” + DA + UR + RA (Harper’s List of Signs no. 109 gives GUD.DA.UR.RA), left unread; the hire for it is four kor of grain a year: idi GU₄.DA.UR.RA “the hire of a GU₄.DA.UR.RA” · Sumerogram, reading not given
4: four — the numeral 4, said erbet (?) before a masculine noun (the spoken form is reconstructed): 4 ŠE.GUR “four kor of grain”
GU₄.LID.UD.SAG: GU₄.LID.UD.SAG, a second named kind of hired ox or team (?), UNCERTAIN: GU₄ “ox” + LID “cow” + UD “day, sun” + SAG “head”, left unread and not guessed at (Harper’s List of Signs no. 109 writes it GU₄.LID.UD.SAG); its hire is three kor of grain · Sumerogram, reading not given
nēšum: lion — written with the two signs UR “dog” + MAḪ “great”: UR.MAḪ, said nēšum; labbum is also “lion” and the signs do not choose between them, UNCERTAIN which word is meant: ina ṣērim UR.MAḪ “a lion in the open country”
mēgūtum: carelessness, negligence (Harper’s sense; UNCERTAIN as a word, the sense is the one the law needs): ina mēgūtim (me-gu-tim) “through carelessness”
šēpum: foot: šēpīšu (NER-šu, the one sign NER “foot” + šu) “his/its foot or feet”; the sign gives no number, so one foot or both is UNCERTAIN (Harper’s List of Signs no. 170, ner, kiš, šēpu)
labiān: labiān-, UNCERTAIN: a word I cannot read, a form-lemma only (no root identified); the law lists it beside the foot of a hired ox, so it is probably a part of the animal, but that is only the context: labiānšu (la-bi-a-an-šu) “its labiān-”, left untranslated
qarnum: horn: qarnīšu (qar-ni-šu) “its horns” (an oblique plural or dual, so “horns”)
zibbatum: tail (ZIB): zibbassu (ZIB-zu, the sign ZU standing for -ssu, zibbat + -šu, t + š said ss) “its tail”
pasuttum: pasuttum, a part of an ox I cannot identify, UNCERTAIN: written with two signs, the corner sign SA and a triangle sign with a diamond and a tail that I could not identify (Harper’s List of Signs no. 50 gives the pair as pasuttu; on the plate the triangle sign comes first), + -šu: pasuttišu “its pasuttu”; šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
nasākum: to throw, cast (UNCERTAIN in the sense used): ittasak (it-ta-sa-ak, perfect) “he has thrown”, taken as “has torn off” from the context; the final sign AK could also be aq, which would be nasāqum “to pick out”
sūqum: street, way (UNCERTAIN): sūqam (zu-ga-am, accusative) “the street”, reading zu for su and ga for qa₂; the z for s spelling is not confirmed
nakkāpum: gorer, a goring (butting) ox (noun from nakāpum “to gore”): nakkāpamma (na-ak-ka-a[m-ma], the last signs restored; the exact form UNCERTAIN) “is a gorer” · nakkapû (na-ak-ka-pu-u) in kīma nakkapû “as a gorer”, the ending -û Harper’s, UNCERTAIN
edûm-Š: Š-stem (causative) of edûm “to know”: to make known, notify: ušēdišumma (u-še-di-šum-ma, preterite + -šum “to him” + -ma) “he made known to him, and”, written as a passive in English because no subject is named
ušarrim: ušarrim (u-šar-ri-im), a D-stem preterite (u-šarrim) of a verb whose root I cannot fix, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only; the sense “trim, cut back (the horns)” is what the context needs and nothing else supports: lā ušarrim “he has not trimmed (?)”
sanāqum: to keep in check (UNCERTAIN: the sense is taken from the context alone): D-stem usanniqma (u-sa-an-ni-iq-ma, preterite + -ma) “he has (not) kept (it) in check, and”; alpīšu lā usanniqma “he has not kept his ox in check (?)”
aldāʾam: aldāʾam, a word I cannot read, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only: aldāʾam (Harper’s al-dá-a-am, accusative ending), taken as farm supplies entrusted to the steward (seed-grain?) from the context alone, left unread
ŠÀ.GAL: ŠÀ.GAL, a Sumerogram of two signs, ŠÀ “heart, inside” + GAL “big”, which I cannot read; “fodder” is the guess from the pairing with seed-grain and cattle, UNCERTAIN: zēr šeʾim ù lu ŠÀ.GAL “seed-grain or fodder (?)” · Sumerogram, reading not given
enēšum-D: D-stem of enēšum “to be weak”: to weaken, make weak: utenniš (u-te-en-ni-iš, 3rd singular preterite; a D perfect would be uttenniš) “he has weakened”, said of cattle; the adjective enšum “weak” is in the prologue
tâna: tâna, a word I cannot read, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma only (Harper’s ta-a-na): it names something measured in grain (the loss, yield or amount?), left as tâna
pīḫatum: pīḫatum, UNCERTAIN: Harper’s bi-ḫa-zu read as pīḫassu (pīḫatum + -šu, t + š said ss, ZU for -ssu) “his pīḫatu”, taken from the context as what he owes; a form-lemma, the root is not clear to me
imtanaššar: imtanaššar-, UNCERTAIN, a form-lemma for an unclear root: a Gtn present of a verb whose root I take as mašārum, a guess, “to drag about” (Harper’s sense): imtanaššarūšu (im-ta-na-aš-ša-ru-šu, present plural + -šu) “they shall drag him about (?)”; the -tan- gives “repeatedly”
AK.ŠU: AK.ŠU, a Sumerogram of two signs, AK + ŠU (Harper lists it under AK, his sign no. 48), a title I cannot read; the context (hired for a year, paid in grain) says a hired worker of some kind, UNCERTAIN · Sumerogram, reading not given
8: eight — the numeral 8 (VIII); said samānat (?) before a masculine noun (the spoken form is reconstructed): 8 ŠE.GUR “eight kor of grain”
1-kam: one, written 1{kam}: the numeral 1 followed by the sign KAM, written raised ({kam}), as in the earlier counts of years; said ištēt (?) with the feminine šattum: MU 1{kam} “one year”, ištēt reconstructed

__broaden__.alpum: ox (GU₄) · forms met: alpam (accusative, GU₄ alone or GU₄ + AM: GU₄-am), alpum (GU₄-um, subject), alpim (genitive, GU₄), alap (construct “ox of”: alap awīlim “a man’s ox”), alpīšu (GU₄-šu) “his ox”; the plate writes the word sometimes GU₄ alone and sometimes with a following sign
__broaden__.idum: hire, wages (Harper: ID, the ideogram for hire): idi našpakim “the hire of the bin”, written with the single sign Á (A₂, “arm; hire”); the case ending is not written, so idi (construct, before a genitive) is an assumed reading, UNCERTAIN · idīšu (Á-šu, with -šu “his”) “his fee”, the physician’s pay: ana asîm idīšu “to the physician as his fee”; the case vowel is UNCERTAIN · Á alone, no ending and no suffix written, before a named kind of ox: idi GU₄.DA.UR.RA “the hire of a GU₄.DA.UR.RA”; the plate sign is Á (A₂), where Harper prints ID
__broaden__.agārum: to hire: īgurma “he hired, and” · īgur (i-gur) “he hired”, without -ma, and īguru (i-gu-ru) “(who) hired”, with the relative -u: awīlum ša alpam īguru “the man who hired the ox”
__broaden__.nakāpum: to gore, butt; munakkip “gorer of” · ikkipma (Harper’s ik-ki-ib-ma, the sign IB read ip; preterite + -ma) “has gored, and”
__broaden__.dâkum: to kill; N-stem iddâk “he shall be killed” — the code’s death sentence · idukkū (i-du-uk-ku) “they shall kill” (active plural, unlike the N-stem iddâk) · iddūkšu (id-du-uk-šu) “has killed him/it”, taken as the perfect + -šu, the doubled d being the perfect’s infix -ta- assimilated to the root’s d (so read; UNCERTAIN in form)
__broaden__.maḫāṣum: to strike; of ground, to break up: imaḫḫaṣ “he shall break up” · the noun maḫāṣum “beating, abuse, injury” (Harper), written ma-ḫa-ṣi-im with the sign ZI (value ṣi): maḫāṣim “(through) beating” · imtaḫaṣ (im-ta-ḫa-aṣ, perfect) “he has struck”, imḫaṣma (preterite + -ma), amḫaṣ “I struck”: amḫassu (am-ḫa-zu) “I struck him” (ṣ + š said ss, written with ZU); the infinitive maḫāṣišu (ma-ḫa-zi-šu) “his striking, his blow”, ina maḫāṣišu “from his blow” · imḫassuma (im-ḫa-zu-ma, preterite imḫaṣ + -šu “him” + -ma, ZU for -ssu) “has struck him, and”, of a god striking an animal dead
__broaden__.nakāsum: to cut, cut down: ikkis (preterite) “he cut down” · inakkisū (i-na-ak-ki-su) “they shall cut off”, present plural (the ending -sū is written with the one sign su, as Harper prints it): lišānšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his tongue”, tulêša inakkisū “they shall cut off her breast” · inakkisū “they shall cut off”, of the hand(s) and the ear: rittēšu inakkisū “they shall cut off his hand(s)”, uznašu inakkisū “they shall cut off his ear” · ittakis (it-ta-ki-is, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has cut (off)”
__broaden__.šebērum: to break: ištebir (iš-te-bi-ir, perfect, 3rd singular) “he has broken”, išebbirū (i-še-ib-bi-ru, present, 3rd plural, with the b doubled) “they shall break” · verb · išbir (iš-bi-ir, preterite, 3rd singular) “he has broken”
__broaden__.šīrum: flesh, body; wellbeing · šīr (SU, bound form before a genitive) “flesh of”: šīr pasuttišu “the flesh of its pasuttu”
__broaden__.1: one — a single vertical wedge (DIŠ): 1 mana “one mina” · ištēt (?) “one” with the feminine šattum, a reconstructed spoken form: ana šattim ištēt “for one year”; also written 1{kam}
__broaden__.3: three — three wedges: šalāš “three” (šalāš šiqil kaspim “three shekels of silver”); the spoken form is reconstructed from the numeral · numeral · šalāšat (?) “three” before a masculine noun (reconstructed): 3 ŠE.GUR “three kor of grain”
__broaden__.-šum: to him, for him (dative suffix -šum, on a verb): ibaššišum “there is to him”, iqbišum “he said to him”, inaddiššum “he shall give him” · after d the suffix is assimilated and spelled ZUM: ipqissum (ip-qi₂-zum) “he entrusted to him” · ušēdišumma (u-še-di-šum-ma) “he made known to him, and”
__broaden__.lū: or; either (lū … lū “whether … or”); with verb: “let …” · ù lu, two words written together, “or”: ù lu ina maḫāṣim “or through beating”
__broaden__.pānum: front, face: ina pani “in front of” · panīša ištakan “she has set her face”: the idiom for making up one’s mind, resolving to do something; with ana + infinitive “to …” (panīšu, panīša “his, her face”) · idioms: panam šakānum “to set the face” = to make up one’s mind; panīšu wabālum “to carry his face” = to overlook an offence (UNCERTAIN) · ana pani X uzuzzim “to stand before X”, i.e. to be in charge of it: ana pani eqlišu uzuzzim “to take charge of his field” (a reading from the sense, UNCERTAIN)
__broaden__.izuzzum: to stand; izzazzu “he stands (in service)” · izzaz, izzazma (i-za-az, i-za-az-ma) “she shall stand (take her place)”, of an heir’s share: zittam kīma aplim ištēn izzazma “she shall take a share like one heir, and”; ul izzaz “she shall have no share”; sense UNCERTAIN · mūzaz (mu-za-az) “one who stands (in service)”, the participle, construct before a genitive: mūzaz ekallim “one who stands in the palace’s service” · uzuzzim (u-zu-uz-zi-im, infinitive, genitive) “to stand (in charge)”: ana pani eqlišu uzuzzim “to take charge of his field”
__broaden__.qiāpum: to entrust, give in trust (Harper “to intrust”, listed under qâpu): iqīp(ma) “he entrusted (the agent), and” · iqīpšu ([i]-qi₂-ip-šu, preterite + -šu, first sign restored, IB read ip) “he has entrusted to him”
__broaden__.paqādum: to entrust, care for; pāqid “caretaker” · ipqissum (ip-qi₂-zum, preterite ipqid + -šum, d + š said ss, ZUM for -ssum) “he has entrusted to him”
__broaden__.erēšum: to ask, demand; also to cultivate: irriš “he demands (his field back)” · erēšim (e-ri-ši-im, infinitive, genitive) “to cultivate”: ana eqlim erēšim “to cultivate the field”
__broaden__.rakāsum-D: D-stem of rakāsum “to bind”: to bind (by agreement), contract with (Harper: “to contract with”): urtakkis (ur-ta-ak-ki-is, perfect, with the t of the perfect after the first sign); who the subject is rests on the context · urakkissu (u-ra-ak-ki-su, D with -šu) “he has bound him (to it)”, the final sign su read for -ssu, UNCERTAIN
__broaden__.šarāqum: to steal: išriq · išriqma (iš-ri-iq-ma, preterite + -ma) “he stole, and”
__broaden__.qātum: hand: ina qāt “from the hand of” · qātīšu (qa₂-ti-šu) “of his hands”: bīš qātīšu “his own goods” · qāt (qa₂-at) construct “in the hand of, in the care of”: ina qāt mušēniqtim “in the care (hand) of the wet-nurse” · qātīšu “of his hands” in šipir qātīšu “the work of his hands” · ina qātišu (qa₂-ti-šu) “in his hand”: ittaṣbat ina qātišu “he was caught with it in his hand”
__broaden__.marārum: to hoe, break clods: imarrar “he shall hoe” · imrirū (im-ri-ru, preterite plural, the ending -ū also serving as the subjunctive) “which they hoed”, UNCERTAIN: the vowel i is not what a preterite beside imarrar would give (imrurū), so the root is in doubt too
__broaden__.zērum: seed; offspring (written with the seed-sign NUMUN) · zēr šeʾim (ŠE.ZIR, the logogram ŠE + ZIR) “seed-grain”
__broaden__.eqlum: field (written A.ŠÀ): eqelšu “his field” — the fief-land this whole block protects · bound form eqel (eqel itêšu “his neighbour’s field”; eqel ušākilu “the field he grazed”) · eqlam (A.ŠÀ, accusative) “the field”, eqlša (A.ŠÀ-ša) “her field”: eqlša u kirâša “her field and her orchard” · eqlišu (A.ŠÀ-šu) “his field”, eqlim (A.ŠÀ-lim, genitive) “of the field, in the field”
__broaden__.bēlum: owner, lord: bēl ḫulqim “owner of the lost property” · owner of a field, bēl eqlim; bēl ḫubullim “creditor” · bēl kirîm “owner of the orchard” · bēl (be-el), the construct “owner of”, also with a suffix on the noun that follows: bēl ḫubullišu “his creditor”, bēl ḫubulliša “her creditor” · bēl (be-el, not the sign EN) “owner of”: bēl aššatim “the owner of the wife”, i.e. the man entitled to her (my reading) · bēlišu (be-li-šu) “its owner” (of an animal), bēlišuma “to its owner only” (with the emphatic -ma); bēl alpim “the owner of the ox”
__broaden__.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver” · kasap (KÙ.BABBAR, no ending written) construct “silver of”: kasap tirḫatim “silver of the bride-price” · kaspi (KÙ.BABBAR, no complement written; Harper’s normalization) in kaspi mišil šīmišu “silver, half its price”
__broaden__.apālum: to answer; to satisfy, pay (a creditor): ippalma (present, with -ma) “he shall pay, and” · uppal (u-up-pa-al) “she shall pay”, taken as a present (a G present would be ippal; the u- is unexplained), in šaniam ul uppal, UNCERTAIN · apālam (a-pa-lam, infinitive, accusative) “to pay”: apālam lā ileʾʾi “he is not able to pay”
__broaden__.ina: in, from · at (ina ebūrim “at harvest”); out of (ina bilat kirîm “out of the orchard’s yield”) · “through, by (means of)”: ina maḫāṣim “through beating”, ina pilšim “by a breach”; “regarding”: ina mimma ša … “regarding whatever …”; ina šanat “in the year” · “with, by”, of company or means (UNCERTAIN): ina liātim “with (or by) the cattle”
